text: Agile methodology is a popular approach to managing projects, especially in software development. Instead of working on a project all at once, teams work in short, focused periods called sprints, which usually last two to four weeks. Each sprint begins with planning, where the team selects tasks from a list of work called a backlog. These tasks are often written as user stories, describing a feature from the perspective of the user. Throughout the sprint, the team holds brief daily meetings known as standups to share progress and discuss any problems or blockers. This emphasis on iterative development allows for regular feedback and adjustments. As a result, teams can adapt to changes quickly, delivering valuable improvements to the product after every sprint, making the process more flexible and efficient than traditional methods.
